target.title: fix(tlon): stop monitor tracking state from growing forever
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a long-running Tlon monitor retained every thread parent ID it had replied in and every DM invite ship it had processed for the full process lifetime. Active installations could therefore accumulate monitor-only identifiers indefinitely as new threads and invitations appeared.

## Why This Change Was Made

Thread participation now uses a dedicated 2,000-entry access-refreshed LRU, matching the existing Tlon processed-message tracking window. Recent threads still accept follow-ups without a mention; after eviction, an old thread requires a direct bot mention again.

DM invite state follows the `/v3` protocol owner instead of using an arbitrary count cap: each invite array is treated as the authoritative active snapshot, removed ships are forgotten, and side effects are deduplicated for every invite still present even when the snapshot contains more than 2,000 ships. Per-ship in-flight work is coalesced so overlapping snapshots wait for the active attempt and retry if it fails.

## User Impact

Long-running Tlon monitors no longer retain thread and DM-invite identifiers forever. Recent thread behavior and active-invite deduplication are preserved; very old participated threads beyond the 2,000-entry window require mentioning the bot again, and an invite that disappears then later reappears is processed as a new active invite.

No configuration, persistence, public SDK, or Tlon wire-format surface changes.

## Evidence

- Focused local Vitest run of `extensions/tlon/src/monitor/tracking.test.ts` and `extensions/tlon/src/monitor/index.tracking.test.ts`: **2 files, 7 tests passed**. Coverage includes thread LRU eviction/recency, exact old-vs-recent thread dispatch after 2,001 participated threads, a 2,001-ship active invite snapshot, full-snapshot duplicate suppression, removal/reappearance, overlapping snapshots, failed work, and rejected work.
- Local E2E live proof ran the production `monitorTlonProvider()` and real `UrbitSSEClient` against a loopback HTTP/SSE Urbit protocol fixture. The monitor subscribed through the real channel endpoint and processed a 2,001-ship `/v3` invite snapshot through real HTTP RSVP pokes. Replaying the full snapshot produced **0 duplicate side effects**; two new ships produced two pokes; removing and reintroducing the oldest ship produced one new poke. Final observation: `totalDmRsvpPokes=2004`, `runtimeErrors=0`.
- The monitor-path thread proof overflowed the 2,000-entry participation window, then sent unmentioned replies to the oldest and newest parents. Only the newest retained parent dispatched.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` passed for all four changed files.
- `git diff --check` passed.

The local machine uses Node 22.17, below the repository's Node 22.19+ floor, so focused Vitest commands were run through a temporary compatibility copy of the repository runner that only replaces the unsupported `import.meta.main` entry guard; project selection and test configuration remained the repository runner's.

AI-assisted: implementation and independent review were performed with coding agents. A local `codex review --base origin/main` could not run because the configured provider credential (`MYAPI_API_KEY`) is unavailable; final independent review found no remaining actionable issues.
